question.text: Himalaya Credit Opportunities Fund (Cat II) exits a LISTED equity position (held 8 months, STT paid) on 15 September 2024 with a gain of INR 2 crore, pass-through to a resident LP. At what rate is this STCG taxed in the LP's hands (ignoring surcharge and cess)?

answer.text: 20% under Section 111A, as amended by Finance (No.2) Act 2024 for transfers on/after 23-07-2024.
Slab rate applicable to the LP.

explanation.text: The Logic: Listed equity held ≤12 months with STT paid is STCG under Section 111A. The Finance (No.2) Act 2024 INCREASED the STCG rate from 15% to 20% for transfers on or after 23-07-2024 (plus surcharge — capped at 15% — and cess). A 15 September 2024 exit falls post the cut-off, so the 20% rate applies. Pass-through preserves this character, so the LP's tax = 2 crore x 20% (plus surcharge up to 15% and cess). The Trap: Option A is the pre-23-07-2024 rate. Option B misclassifies the 8-month holding as LTCG (needs >12 months). Option D applies ordinary slab, ignoring the special-rate regime under Section 111A. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests both the 20% STCG and the 12.5% LTCG together. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) heavily tests Section 111A because PMS is listed-equity dominated. XIX-A uses it in client tax-planning scenarios. Remember: 111A requires STT AND a recognised stock exchange. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat II debt-hybrids that opportunistically trade listed equity, revisit your fund's frequency of listed-equity trading post-FA 2025 (Sec 2(14) amendment deems such securities capital assets for Cat I/II). This removes the 'business income' risk and locks in 111A/112A treatment.
